sourceLine: your Texas DPS and Interceptor work, and the questions agencies ask before they buy VR training

cards.title: Offline VR Is the Real Procurement Requirement
cards.angle: Texas DPS selected OP-2 in August 2025 for a statewide deployment, and agency IT reviews turn heavily on connectivity, updates and where training data lives. Running multi-user tracked scenarios with real-weapon recoil on standalone headsets is what makes those answers easy.
cards.evidence: OP-2 carries its own offline claims and shipped to Texas DPS on an initial AUD 4.3M order, up to AUD 5.71M with options; Interceptor, a separate product, runs with no backpack PC, no external tracking, no WiFi, at about 23 kg per two users. Your insights posts cover growth and events; the offline-architecture piece is the one a procurement officer forwards.

cards.title: Counter-Drone Training Outruns Live Ranges
cards.angle: Live exercises cannot conveniently reproduce every drone threat or electronic-warfare condition, and counter-UAS skills decay without reps. The useful question is which decisions teams can rehearse in simulation and what still has to be tested in the field.
cards.evidence: Interceptor launched in April 2026 with FPV, ISR and swarm scenarios and EW effects, and a non-binding MOU with Thales Australia followed in June. Your ADM feature argues for simulated runs before live evaluation; the piece underneath it is how you decide what the simulation has to get right.

cards.title: Grant-Funded VR Needs a Plan Past the Purchase
cards.angle: DOJ's FY2026 Safer Outcomes program funded agency awards in capped, time-limited tracks. A grant buys the kit; keeping scenarios current, training instructors and maintaining equipment needs a budget line that outlives it, and most vendors avoid saying so.
cards.evidence: Your parent company reports a growing base of agency clients and a recurring-revenue model built on scenarios, analytics and support. A plain piece on how an agency should budget beyond the grant year is one no competitor has written, and it positions the subscription as the point rather than the catch.
